title: Aaron Levie on AI's Enterprise Adoption

reader_summary.headline: What is the journey over the next decade?
reader_summary.overview: What is the journey over the next decade? It's about the speed at which humans can change their workflows. Why doesn't the breakthrough that we just saw get released? Why isn't that permeate every corporation within six months?

key_points.text: It's so strange to me how many disruptions are happening all at the same time.
key_points.evidence_quote: It's so strange to me how many disruptions are happening all at the same time.

key_points.text: We're not in like a fear of AI world.
key_points.evidence_quote: We're not in like a fear of AI world.

key_points.text: We know this is going to happen and it needs to happen to us faster than it happens in our competitors.
key_points.evidence_quote: We know this is going to happen and it needs to happen to us faster than it happens in our competitors, which is a totally different dynamic than we saw in Cloud.

positions.commentary: The speaker believes that Box's durability is tied to its ability to teach users workflows, making it resistant to being replaced by AI.

thesis: The episode argues that vertical SaaS companies like Box possess significant durability against AI disruption because they combine deep domain expertise with complex, hard-to-rebuild core infrastructure. The speaker contends that these firms are resistant to replacement because they teach users specific workflows and handle unstructured data, rather than relying on generic prompts or 'vibe coding' to build agents.

claims.claim: The speaker believes Box has significant durability because it understands specific workflows and domain expertise, which pure horizontal AI systems cannot easily replicate.
claims.quote: And then I think the other thing- I still think that there's a relationship between some amount of GUI and the agent and the APIs, because again, like, you don't want it every day of your life go to a blank empty screen and say, what's our revenue today? You just want to dashboard at some point and just show us the revenue.

claims.claim: The speaker states that Box AI deals with unstructured data and can be used to improve earnings scripts by injecting answers to analyst questions.
claims.quote: And then, again, because box AI deals with unstructured data, I just load up the earnings script and I'll use a better model and say, give me 10 points that analysts are going to ask about this and, like, how would I improve the script?

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Box has about 120,000 customers, representing about 65 percent of the Fortune 500.
claims.quote: We have about 120,000 customers, about 65 or so percent of the fortune of 500.

claims.claim: The speaker believes that vertical SaaS companies like Box have trivial technology but deep domain understanding that makes them durable against AI disruption.
claims.quote: I mean, I would say most vertical SaaS companies I see, the technology's trivial. Yeah, but the understanding of the domain is not-

claims.claim: The speaker suggests that Box's core infrastructure, like storing data, is hard to rebuild and cannot be easily vibe coded away.
claims.quote: So like, okay, so I can imagine why it would be hard to rebuild box because what you do is actually hard. This is core infrastructure, your store data, like that's really important.

claims.claim: The speaker believes that vertical players will continue to do domain-specific work rather than relying on prompts to build agents, citing FDA compliance as an example.
claims.quote: Now, that translates fine to agents, but I still would then bet on that vertical player doing that as opposed to somebody prompts their way in the chat to BT to build a FDA compliance agent.
